text:
Marathon Petroleum has climbed 9.6% over two weeks, with today's modest 0.7% gain capping a sharp four-day rally that started around September 14th. The timing lines up with escalating Middle East tensions—Houthi attacks, reports of strikes near Saudi airports, and Iran closing the Strait of Hormuz—which typically tighten global oil supplies and support refiner margins. US crude has held around $107 per barrel while global crude sits at $130, and refineries are running near capacity at 96.8%, a posture that benefits processors when crude costs rise and demand stays steady.

This rally reflects the refining sector's sweet spot when geopolitical risk pushes oil prices higher but doesn't collapse demand; the gap between the world price and US price suggests supply tightness abroad, which can improve the value of US refinery output. With storage levels moderate (708 million barrels of oil, 208 million of gasoline), the market is pricing in continued strength from both elevated crude costs and the structural advantage of operating at full capacity during supply-constrained periods.
